summary: 1. Sep 23 lands essentially flat against the production target (-0.13%), but every BCM moved was waste — ore came in at zero for the first time this article has tracked, a seventh consecutive ore-target miss. 2. Total 20,615 BCM against a 20,641 BCM target; waste alone beat its own target by 9.86%. 3. MTD holds at +6.24% (614,017 BCM), narrowing from Sep 22's +6.48% as the zero-ore day drags the ore surplus down further. 4. Crusher stockpile throughput lifts to 36.09% of the monthly plan as downtime recovers sharply from Sep 22's 13h10m (the worst logged in this article) to 2h49m. 5. Fleet-wide, Overall Daily availability eased to 87.78% and Core Fleet Daily to 81.14% as EX-253 completes an eighth full day down and EX-123 a second full day down on its Hydraulic Oil Leaking fault, while DT-108's 2,000-hour service closes and a first-time fault opens on Track Dozer DZ-248 (Track Completely Worn-out). 6. See [[daily-production-report]] and [[fleet-availability-utilization]]. 2. 7. A blast-reporting discrepancy surfaces between two tabs of the same workbook: the Sept (23) tab's own Yesterday-Blast field records Blast #20 firing on Sep 22 (860_517+518, 36,124 BCM), directly contradicting the Sept (22) tab's own same-day production block, which this KB already compiled as "No blast fired." Not resolved this pass. 3. 8. A new Non-Conformance Report (HSEQ-NCR-ADW-26-021) records a second Line-of-Fire/50:30:10 HME Approach Rule finding against Production Supervisor Richard Meager, dated the night of 22-Sep, one day after the Excavator-398 approach incident already under active investigation in this KB for the same supervisor and the same rule. 9. Peter's own Project Manager comment on the form recommends a formal disciplinary review "including consideration of termination of employment," citing a reported history of prior speeding violations and verbal warnings. Does the zero-ore day reflect a genuine face-sequencing gap or a one-day allocation choice to run waste-only? Worth checking against the next populated tab and [[blasting-and-drilling]]. Does EX-123's Hydraulic Oil Leaking fault, now two full days down, become a second standing multi-week excavator stoppage alongside EX-253? Does DZ-248's Track Completely Worn-out fault clear quickly, or become the ancillary fleet's next standing multi-day stoppage? Which blast record is right on Sep 22 — the production tab's "No blast fired," or the following day's "Yesterday Blast" entry for Blast #20? Is the new NCR against Richard Meager a second, separate incident from the Excavator-398 investigation, or a restatement of the same event under a different reporting form? This needs Peter's read before it goes anywhere in the Wiki, given the termination recommendation already on the record. Carried forward — does the D8 dozer loan request get resolved by Saturday, and does it change WD-145's repair priority (58 days down and counting)? Source: `Production report/Sep 26/September Client Meeting Report.xlsx` (Sept (23) tab); `Maintanance Shedules/Sep 26/DailyAvailability_Final_Report (23-09-2025 ).pdf`; `NCR/NCR - Richard.pdf`; `Maintanance Shedules/Sep 26/RE Planned work for Friday 250902026.msg`. `September Block Info.xlsx`, `September A & U.xlsx`, `DPR-September-2026.xlsx`, `September Daily Drill Meters Report.xlsx`, `Equipment running hours report -.xlsx`, and `DPR and A&U- September.docx` registered, cross-check only. No new survey workbook landed this pass. Tasks: none created this pass. The NCR item above is a judgment call flagged for Peter directly rather than turned into a standalone task; the rest of the open items are logged in the affected articles' own Open Questions sections. [[survey-volume-reconciliation]] was not touched — no new survey workbook landed since the last pass. Important References, Notes & References, and Task Feedback Log workflows were not run this pass, per the task's own instructions (they ran in the prior day's full-scope pass). No content removed or renamed from RAW. ---
